about: The AP Psychology app pages. scripts/build-appsych.mjs writes each page's shell (head, header, footer, a <div id="app"> mount) from this file; the page's behavior is its script in psychology/assets/<script>, which mounts into #app. "static": true marks a generated page that is not an app (teachers.html). premium names the Premium feature (ApPsychCore gates it); card is the line on the course home. No path may contain the token "ap" (docs/appsych-spec.md decision 2). tools[] are the ten trainers of docs/appsych-spec.md section 6, pre-registered in Phase 0: page psychology/tools/<slug>.html, script psychology/assets/tools/<slug>.js, model psychology/assets/tools/math/<slug>.js (ApPsychMath.<camelSlug>), content psychology/data/tools/<slug>.json, validator scripts/lib/appsych-tool-checks/<slug>.mjs, test scripts/test/appsych-tool-<slug>.test.mjs (docs/appsych-architecture.md, "Tools"). topic is the tool's context topic: the tool is built only when its data file exists and that topic is published. FREE OR PREMIUM is set here and only here: a tool with "premium": "tools" is Premium; article-studio, neuron and brain-map carry none and are free (docs/appsych-spec.md section 6, proposed; owner to confirm).

apps.title: Practice questions
apps.desc: Psychology practice by unit, topic or skill: study, data and figure sets, concepts applied to new situations, and answers made specific.
apps.card: Drill a unit, a topic or a skill, with study, data and figure sets.

apps.title: Spaced review
apps.desc: Your psychology spaced review queue: every question you missed comes back just before you would forget it.
apps.card: Missed questions come back when you are about to forget them.

apps.title: Unit tests and practice exams
apps.desc: Timed psychology unit tests and full practice exams in the May 2027 format: 75 multiple-choice questions, then the article analysis and evidence-based questions.
apps.card: Unit tests and full timed practice exams in the May 2027 format.

apps.title: Free-response practice
apps.desc: Psychology free-response practice in the two exam question types, the article analysis and the evidence-based question, 7 points each, with a rubric and a full-credit sample.
apps.card: The article analysis and evidence-based questions, with 7-point rubrics and sample answers.

apps.title: Make it specific
apps.desc: Psychology written answers made specific enough to score: the research method, operational definitions, claims, cited evidence and the concept that links them.
apps.lede: Write the answer, then check it against the rubric and two model answers: one that earns the point and one that loses it.
apps.card: Methods, operational definitions, claims and cited evidence specific enough to score, checked against a rubric.

apps.title: Cram kit
apps.desc: Psychology cram plans counted back from your exam date: three or two weeks, day by day, weighted by unit, with timed sets and practice exams.
apps.lede: A 3-week or 2-week plan counted back from your exam date, day by day: unit sheets and notes, a timed mixed set and one free-response question each study day, two full practice exams and rest days. Print it and tick the days off.
apps.card: 3-week and 2-week plans to exam day, and timed mixed sets.

apps.title: Flashcards
apps.desc: Spaced-repetition psychology flashcards built from the glossary and the statistics you must know, by unit and topic.
apps.card: Spaced-repetition cards from the glossary and the statistics.

apps.title: Trainers
apps.desc: Psychology trainers: article analysis, evidence, the neuron, the brain, sensation, memory, conditioning, development, social influence and statistics.
apps.card: Trainers and simulators, then the questions about what you saw.

apps.title: Your dashboard
apps.desc: Your psychology mastery by unit, topic and skill, with every miss linked to the lesson that teaches it.
apps.card: Mastery by unit, topic and skill.

apps.title: Search the course
apps.desc: Search every psychology lesson, notes page, glossary term and tool in the course.

apps.title: For teachers
apps.desc: For psychology teachers: stable share links, printable notes and unit sheets, and Google Classroom sharing, with no new student data collected.
apps.lede: Share any notes page, lesson or unit sheet with a stable link. Students need no account, and nothing they do leaves their device unless they choose to sign in.

tools.name: Article analysis studio
tools.title: Article Analysis Studio
tools.desc: The article analysis question made drillable: a study summary taken apart part by part (method, operational definition, statistic, ethics, generalizability, argument), each graded with the slip named.
tools.blurb: A study summary taken apart, part by part, as the AAQ asks.
tools.lede: Read the study, then answer each part the way the readers score it.

tools.name: Evidence builder
tools.title: Evidence Builder
tools.desc: The evidence-based question made drillable: three short sources, a claim, evidence from the right source with its citation, and a psychology concept that links them.
tools.blurb: Claim, evidence from the right source, and a concept that links them.
tools.lede: Build a claim, cite the evidence, then link it with a concept.

tools.name: Neuron
tools.title: The Neuron
tools.desc: Fire a neuron: threshold, the all-or-none action potential, the refractory period, and what agonists, antagonists and reuptake inhibitors do at the synapse.
tools.blurb: Fire an action potential and see what a drug does at the synapse.
tools.lede: Push a neuron past threshold, then change what happens at the synapse.

tools.name: Brain map
tools.title: Brain Map
tools.desc: The brain region by region: tap a structure or a lobe to see what it does, then read lesion, imaging and split-brain cases and name the region.
tools.blurb: Tap a region to see what it does, and what damage there changes.
tools.lede: Tap a region, then name it from a case.

tools.name: Sensation and perception
tools.title: Sensation and Perception
tools.desc: Absolute and difference thresholds, signal detection, sensory adaptation, and the perceptual cues and illusions the exam uses.
tools.blurb: Thresholds, signal detection and the illusions that fool you.
tools.lede: Find a threshold, then see what top-down processing changes.

tools.name: Memory lab
tools.title: Memory Lab
tools.desc: Encoding, storage and retrieval: the serial position curve, the spacing effect, interference and forgetting, from your own recall.
tools.blurb: Encode, store and retrieve, and watch interference at work.
tools.lede: Learn a list, then see what helped and what got in the way.

tools.name: Conditioning lab
tools.title: Conditioning Lab
tools.desc: Classical conditioning from acquisition to spontaneous recovery, and operant conditioning: reinforcement and punishment, and the four schedules with their response curves.
tools.blurb: Pair a tone with food, then reinforce on four schedules.
tools.lede: Condition a response, then change the schedule.

tools.name: Development
tools.title: Development Across the Lifespan
tools.desc: A lifespan timeline: cognitive development stages, attachment and parenting styles, the psychosocial stages and adolescence to adulthood, each placed and applied.
tools.blurb: A lifespan timeline from infancy to old age.
tools.lede: Place each milestone, then apply it to a person.

tools.name: Social influence
tools.title: Social Influence
tools.desc: Attribution, conformity, obedience and group effects: change the situation and predict the behavior, then name the concept.
tools.blurb: Conformity, obedience and the bystander effect, situation by situation.
tools.lede: Change the situation, then predict what people do.

tools.name: Stats lab
tools.title: Stats Lab
tools.desc: The normal curve with the 68-95-99.7 rule, z scores and percentile ranks, central tendency and variation, and correlation from a scatterplot, all worked by hand.
tools.blurb: The normal curve, percentiles and correlation, worked by hand.
tools.lede: Move a score along the curve, then read its percentile.
